exercise.name: 3 Leg Chaturanga Pose
aliases: Eka Pada Chaturanga Dandasana from three-legged dog

reference.title: 3 Leg Chaturanga Pose (female)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored or copied; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.type: Yoga flow: bodyweight upper-body strength plus hamstring and calf mobility
exercise.bodyPart: Upper body (triceps, chest, shoulders) and core
secondaryBodyParts: Glutes and hamstrings of the lifted leg
Hamstrings and calves (lengthened in downward dog)
exercise.laterality: Unilateral leg lift (alternate legs between reps); arms work together

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Controls the lowering into chaturanga and holds the elbows near a right angle (inferred from the push-up shape; no chaturanga EMG found).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Same role on the left arm; both arms share the load.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Lowers and holds the body, as at the bottom of a push-up.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Lowers and holds the body, as at the bottom of a push-up.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm as the body lowers between the hands.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm as the body lowers between the hands.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the lifted right leg in hip extension from three-legged dog through the lowering.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Helps hold the right leg up and straight behind.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade on the rib cage in dog and chaturanga; experts in a 2024 EMG abstract relied on it more than intermediates.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Draws the upper arm back and steadies the lowering; about 35% MVC in the closest Surya Namaskar poses.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keeps the trunk in one line in plank, dog and chaturanga.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keeps the trunk in one line and stops the pelvis turning toward the lifted leg.
muscleNotes.core: Brace so the hips neither sag nor pike while only three, then two, limbs touch the floor.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the back of the shoulder at the bottom.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Steadies the back of the shoulder at the bottom.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis square over the single standing leg.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the lifted hip from opening toward the ceiling.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keeps the standing knee straight in plank and chaturanga.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Lengthens in downward dog; heels stay lifted in this version.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Lengthens in downward dog before the leg lifts.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hips lift up and back to downward dog; inhale as the right leg lifts; keep breathing as you shift forward; exhale to lower into chaturanga; inhale to press back to plank as the leg comes down. Never hold the breath while lowering.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s to dog, 1 s to lift the leg, 1.2 s forward, 1.1 s to lower, a short pause, 1.1 s back to plank

prescription.tempo: Lower in about 2–3 s in practice (faster in the loop shown)
prescription.holds: Optional: 2–3 breaths in three-legged dog; 1 breath at the bottom of chaturanga
prescription.frequency: 2–4 days a week, in a flow or warm-up
prescription.stopRule: End the set when the shoulders start to drop below the elbows

cues.text: High plank: hands under the shoulders, fingers spread, body in one line from head to heels.
Breathe out and press the floor away, lifting the hips up and back into downward dog. Arms and back form one long line.
Breathe in and lift the right leg straight up behind you, in line with the trunk. Both hip points keep facing the floor.
Keep the leg up and shift forward, rolling over the left toes, until the shoulders are ahead of the wrists.
Breathe out and bend the elbows straight back, hugging them to the ribs. Lower until the shoulders reach elbow height.
Pause with the torso level with the elbows; the right leg stays lifted, the hips stay square.
Breathe in and press back up to plank, bringing the right foot back down to the mat.
Reset the plank, then repeat with the left leg.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the chest below the elbows
mistakes.fix: Stop when the shoulders reach elbow height; a block under the sternum or a strap above the elbows teaches the depth.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Hug the elbows to the ribs, pointing straight back.
Move the shoulders ahead of the wrists before the elbows bend, so the forearms stay close to vertical.

mistakes.mistake: Lifted leg swings up and the hip opens
mistakes.fix: Lift only as high as the hips stay level and square to the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging or piking in plank and chaturanga
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk so the body stays in one line.

mistakes.mistake: Weight sinking into the heel of the hand
mistakes.fix: Press through the finger pads, especially the base of the index finger; spread the fingers.
Press the floor away and keep the shoulder blades wide and away from the ears.

kinematics.norm: About 90°, elbows close to the ribs; going lower (eight-limb pose) measured 116 ± 17°

kinematics.peak: ≈15 cm ahead of the wrists at the bottom
kinematics.norm: Shoulders move ahead of the wrists before the elbows bend; torso level with the elbows
Inverted V, trunk and thighs close to a right angle (estimate; no measured norm)

kinematics.peak: In line with the trunk in three-legged dog (hip ≈5°); 12° above the body line in chaturanga
kinematics.norm: Roughly in line with the trunk, hips level (no source verified)

kinematics.peak: ≈84° in plank, ≈42° in dog, ≈71° at the bottom of chaturanga
kinematics.norm: Dog about 50°, hand balances about 90°; eight-limb pose measured 85 ± 13°

kinematics.setup: On the ball of the foot, heel lifted
kinematics.peak: Rolls forward over the toes for the shift, back for plank
kinematics.norm: Practitioners roll onto the tips of the toes to bring the shoulders ahead of the wrists

cautions: Wrist pain, numbness or night tingling (carpal tunnel signs) or wrist arthritis: plank and chaturanga need near-maximal wrist extension; modify or skip.
Shoulder pain or a history of impingement or rotator cuff strain: avoid dropping below elbow height and avoid elbow flare.
Pregnancy: no data on chaturanga or the leg-lifted version; use the knees-down version or skip chaturanga later in pregnancy and check with a prenatal provider.
Stop if lowering causes sharp shoulder or wrist pain.
modify: Lower the knees to the mat for the chaturanga part.
Place a block under the sternum or a strap just above the elbows to set the depth.
Wedge or folded blanket under the heel of the hand; forearm plank or dolphin instead of downward dog.
With both shoulder and wrist problems, replace chaturanga with locust.
regressions: Two-legged chaturanga from plank (no leg lift).
Downward dog to plank only, without the lowering.
progressions: Hold chaturanga for a full breath with the leg lifted.
Hold three-legged dog for 3 breaths before shifting forward.
